page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.4xlarge is a shared-resource compute-oriented instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The architecture supports x86_64 instruction sets, including AVX-512 and hardware AES acceleration. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. Local disk storage is not bundled, necessitating reliance on network-attached block storage, while network interfaces provide a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear divergence between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. Single-core evaluations reflect poor performance, scoring 828.0 in Geekbench and 1072.98 in stress-ng, accompanied by bottom-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (18.63 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (6.67 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregated multi-threaded operations reach average industry ranges, recording a PassMark CPU score of 17422.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6154.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 95.18 GB/sec with 50.04 GB/sec write bandwidth, though overall PassMark memory performance remains weak.

The qualitative tradeoff of the ecs.n4.4xlarge centers on its shared CPU topology and older processor architecture. Because vCPUs are shared rather than dedicated, throughput may fluctuate depending on host load, making the instance less cost-effective for latency-sensitive transactions or high single-core demands. However, for aggregate throughput tasks, it offers an economical distribution of multi-core capacity per resource unit.

Given its performance profile, this instance is appropriate for distributed batch tasks, general microservices, static web serving (benchmarked at 9.83 GB/sec), multi-threaded build systems, and secondary development or test environments where dedicated CPU guarantees and local high-speed NVMe storage are not required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.4xlarge is a shared-resource virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 16 shared vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 compute-optimized memory ratio without included local storage or GPU accelerators. Network baseline throughput is rated at 2 Gbps. While single-thread benchmarks place the instance in lower percentiles due to modest clock speeds and shared hardware scheduling, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU (17422.69) and multi-core Geekbench (6154.0) achieve solid mid-tier output. Without bundled ephemeral disks, primary storage depends on network volumes. This configuration suits distributed background processing, software compilation, static web hosting, and budget-conscious development workloads where strict per-core execution consistency is not a core requirement.
